title: ReLoRA basis rotation with shared butterfly View schedule
hypothesis: A shared butterfly angle schedule plus one scalar Mirror coordinate per restart generates diverse rank-4 update subspaces with lower full payload bytes than independent ReLoRA/BOFT factors while recovering rank-16 quality; any gain must beat the native shared-angle BOFT control.
physical_object: One rank-4 seed basis and a shared five-stage butterfly angle table
mirror_coordinate: One scalar per restart scaling the shared butterfly angles
logical_multiplicity: Four phase-specific rank-4 update subspaces composing a rank-16 cumulative update

task.metric: Relative Frobenius error, effective rank, actual serialized inference bytes, restart representation bytes, rotation/decode MAC proxy

controls: ReLoRA plus independent per-phase BOFT angle tables
Mirror shared butterfly schedule plus per-phase scalar coordinates
Native shared-angle BOFT with the same shared schedule and phase scalars
Static unrotated rank-4 basis boundary control

paid_objects: phase scalars or independent angle tables

success_gate: Mirror relative error <=1e-5, effective rank >=16, complete inference payload <=90% of independent ReLoRA, and strict gain over native shared-angle BOFT in bytes, quality or compute.
failure_gate: Quality/rank/byte miss, or exact alias to native shared-angle BOFT without strict Mirror-specific gain. Fresh seeds remain sealed.
boundaries: No optimizer training or ReLoRA convergence claim
The angle table and its code decoder are fully serialized and charged
No dense orthogonal transform is considered free
